pages.title: About
pages.content:
Since 2014

About Kaze Clinic

Founded in 2014 by Dr. Ines Halvorsen, Kaze Clinic is an independent respiratory medicine clinic in Northmere dedicated entirely to breathing. We combine precise diagnostic measurement with calm, collaborative care that stays with you over time.

Our clinic

Why We Measure First

Breathlessness and chronic cough are frequently treated with trial inhalers before anyone observes lung mechanics. At Kaze Clinic, founded in 2014 by Dr. Ines Halvorsen, we chose to focus exclusively on respiratory medicine so patients never have to guess whether a treatment is working. Breathing symptoms can arise from airway inflammation, restricted lung volume, post-viral sensitivity, or disordered breathing patterns. This diagnostic clarity allows our physicians to target treatments precisely, de-escalate unneeded medications, and ensure you leave with an unambiguous understanding of your lungs.

Why we measure first

By measuring airway caliber and airflow limitation before prescribing, we base every clinical decision on objective physiological data rather than assumptions.

Read about your first visit

How we work

Our core clinical values

Measure first
Spirometry before prescription

We test lung function during your initial appointment so treatment begins with verified baseline figures rather than guesswork.

Agree it in writing
Shared care plan

Every diagnosis, medicine adjustment, and daily recommendation is recorded on a clear paper document written in plain language that you take home.

Someone stays
Named nurse

You are paired with a dedicated respiratory nurse specialist who reviews your progress, checks your inhaler technique, and coordinates your ongoing care over the following weeks.

Daily routine

A day at Kaze Clinic

Our clinic routine follows a predictable schedule to maintain thorough, unhurried consultations.

08:00
Morning huddle

At 08:00, our multidisciplinary team gathers for the morning clinical huddle to review incoming cases and test schedules.

08:30
First tests

At 08:30, our doors open for the first diagnostic tests, including spirometry and FeNO assessments.

Daytime
Consultations

Throughout the day, Dr. Ines Halvorsen and Dr. Kwame Asante conduct 45-minute first consultations and 25-minute reviews.

Thursday evening
Evening clinic

On Thursdays, we host our evening clinic until 20:00 to accommodate working schedules.

17:30
Follow-up calls

Each weekday concludes between 17:30 and 18:00 with dedicated follow-up phone calls, where our nurses review patient progress and answer questions.

pages.title: Conditions
pages.content:
What we see

Conditions we see

We investigate and manage symptoms affecting the airways, lungs, and nighttime breathing. Our consultations connect your daily symptoms to objective physiological measurements.

Seven reasons people arrive

Plain words first, the clinical term beside it

Breathlessness
Dyspnoea

Breathlessness often develops gradually, whether while climbing stairs or during normal exertion, leaving people unsure when fatigue crossed into respiratory restriction. We perform spirometry on the day of your visit to measure whether air moves freely through the bronchial tree or meets narrowing.

Book a first visit

Wheeze and asthma
Asthma review

Wheezing, chest tightness, and exercise-induced coughing frequently point toward asthma or allergic airway inflammation. During an asthma review, we evaluate both your airflow reversibility and FeNO levels to quantify fractional exhaled nitric oxide in the breath. This identifies active eosinophilic inflammation and reveals whether your inhaled preventer dosage is appropriate.

Book a first visit

COPD follow-up
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

For chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, our care combines spirometric surveillance with breathing rehabilitation courses to rebuild functional capacity.

Book a first visit

Persistent cough
Chronic cough

Persistent cough is another frequent reason for referral to our Northmere clinic. Rather than offering repetitive cough syrups, we systematically check for airway hyperresponsiveness, ongoing post-infectious irritation, or upper airway triggers. We isolate the exact mechanism behind the cough reflex so targeted care can quiet the bronchial lining and restore comfort.

Sleep breathing
Sleep apnoea screening

Disordered sleep breathing profoundly affects daytime stamina and general health. For patients experiencing heavy snoring, daytime fatigue, or witnessed pauses in breathing, we conduct sleep apnoea screening using overnight home respiratory polygraphy.

Cough after an infection
Post-viral cough

For a cough that lingers for weeks after a respiratory infection, we assess airway stability and provide a structured plan to soothe sensitized cough receptors and restore steady breathing.

Allergy questions
Allergic airway disease

For patients with seasonal flare-ups or airborne triggers, we address allergic airway disease concurrently. We review inhaler technique with a nurse to confirm the medicine reaches bronchial tissue, adjusting device selection and spacing chambers to resolve persistent nighttime waking and exercise limitation.

pages.title: Tests
pages.content:
Lung function

Lung function and sleep tests

Diagnostic testing at Kaze Clinic is calm, non-invasive, and completed without clinical rush. We explain what each test measures, how it feels, and how to prepare beforehand.

Four tests

What each one feels like

Spirometry
Lung function with reversibility

Spirometry measures how much air your lungs can hold and how rapidly you can exhale it. You will sit comfortably, place a soft clip on your nose, and blow forcefully through a clean, single-use mouthpiece into a sensor guided by respiratory physiologist Tomás Reyes. To assess reversibility, we repeat the measurement after administering a bronchodilator to check if narrowed airways open. The complete assessment takes place during your 45-minute consultation. Please avoid heavy meals and vigorous exercise immediately before testing, and follow the pre-test inhaler instructions provided by our reception team when booking.

FeNO
Airway inflammation

FeNO testing measures fractional exhaled nitric oxide, an established indicator of eosinophilic airway inflammation commonly associated with asthma. During the test, you inhale deeply through a filtered device and exhale steadily at a gentle, continuous pace against light resistance. It feels completely effortless, requiring no forced exhalation, and takes only a few minutes during your appointment. To prepare, please refrain from eating, drinking anything other than plain water, smoking, or vigorous exertion for an hour before testing, ensuring your measurement reflects an accurate baseline of airway activity.

Overnight oximetry
Oxygen saturation

For sleep breathing assessments, we provide lightweight diagnostic equipment to use in your own bed. Overnight oximetry tracks pulse and oxygen saturation through a small fingertip sensor worn while you sleep.

Home sleep study
Respiratory polygraphy

A home sleep study (respiratory polygraphy) records nasal airflow, chest breathing effort, body position, and oxygen levels using a compact unit worn on a soft chest band. You collect the kit from reception, sleep in your usual surroundings for one night, and return the device the following morning for report analysis. Please wear comfortable sleepwear and avoid alcohol on the test night.

Book a first visit

pages.title: Your first visit
pages.content:
Plan

Your first visit

We believe a first respiratory appointment should provide clarity, objective measurements, and a practical plan you understand. Here is what to expect from arrival to follow-up.

Four steps

The four steps of your first plan

Your initial pathway at Kaze Clinic follows four structured steps designed to establish steady breathing.

01 Listen
45-minute first consultation

An unhurried first consultation with Dr. Ines Halvorsen or Dr. Kwame Asante to explore your symptoms, medical history, and daily environment.

02 Measure
Spirometry the same day

Spirometry follows immediately on the same day, alongside FeNO or other physiological testing if needed.

03 Agree
A written plan to take home

We translate clinical findings into a written care plan created in plain language.

04 Stay with it
A named nurse

You are paired with a named nurse, followed by a telephone check-in at 2 weeks and a review at 6 weeks.

What to bring
For the 45 minutes

To help us understand your baseline health, please bring all current respiratory inhalers, spacers, oral medications, and any recent prescriptions. If you have previous chest imaging, lung function reports, allergy test results, or hospital letters, bringing copies is very helpful, alongside any peak flow readings you keep. We also suggest wearing comfortable clothing that does not restrict your chest or abdomen during spirometry testing. Writing down a list of your daily symptoms, questions, and specific breathing triggers ensures that every practical concern is thoroughly reviewed during your 45-minute consultation.

What you leave with

You will never leave Kaze Clinic with unanswered questions or vague advice. You leave with measurable clarity, practical instructions, and an ongoing clinical team committed to keeping your breathing steady.

Book a first visit

At the conclusion of your visit, practice manager Sofia Lindqvist and your respiratory nurse hand you a printed, plain-language care plan detailing your verified test measurements, prescribed therapies, and correct inhaler techniques. The document clearly outlines what steps to take if your symptoms flare, details your named nurse contact, and notes your scheduled 2-week telephone check-in and 6-week review appointment.

pages.title: Clinicians
pages.content:
People

Clinicians

Our multidisciplinary team combines specialist medical expertise, physiological diagnostics, nursing care, physiotherapy, and pharmacy. We collaborate closely on every case to provide cohesive respiratory management.

Seven people

Who you will meet

Dr. Ines Halvorsen
Founder and respiratory physician

She founded Kaze Clinic in 2014 to ensure patients with breathlessness and cough receive objective physiological testing alongside calm, thorough consultations. Her practice centres on diagnostic precision and collaborative care plans that patients understand.

Dr. Kwame Asante
Respiratory physician, sleep breathing

He leads our sleep-disordered breathing and nocturnal hypoxemia assessments, helping patients regain daytime stamina through structured nighttime investigations. His clinical focus includes complex asthma and home sleep studies.

Tomás Reyes
Respiratory physiologist

He conducts diagnostic spirometry, reversibility testing, and FeNO assessments with patience and care. His careful guidance helps patients perform accurate breathing maneuvers comfortably.

Sofia Lindqvist
Practice manager

She oversees patient coordination, scheduling, and clinic administration at 18 Linden Walk. Sofia ensures every appointment runs smoothly, coordinates welcome documentation, and provides itemised receipts for insurance reimbursement with clarity and efficiency.

Priya Raman
Respiratory physiotherapist

She directs our 6-week breathing rehabilitation courses, teaching breathing mechanics, pacing strategies, and conditioning exercises. Her supportive sessions rebuild physical stamina and daily confidence for individuals living with COPD or exertional breathlessness.

Daniel Okoro
Clinical pharmacist

He provides detailed inhaler and medicine reviews, assessing device suitability, drug interactions, and adherence. Daniel ensures every patient understands the precise mechanism of their prescribed medication and can use their delivery device effectively.

Named nurse

Lena Park

She guides patients through daily treatment routines, device choices, and ongoing symptom management. Lena leads our inhaler technique reviews and conducts our weekday follow-up telephone calls between 17:30 and 18:00, ensuring every patient has a dedicated, approachable clinician staying with their case.

Respiratory nurse specialist

pages.title: Fees
pages.content:
Self-pay

Fees

We maintain transparent, fixed pricing for all consultations, diagnostic investigations, and therapy courses. All appointments are self-pay, with itemised receipts provided for insurance claims.

Fee schedule

Consultation and diagnostic fees

We believe clinical pricing should be clear and predictable before you arrive.

Cancellation is free up to 24 hours before your appointment. Many insurers reimburse our fees, and we provide an itemised receipt following every visit.

Insurance
Does private health insurance cover consultations?

Kaze Clinic operates on an independent self-pay basis, allowing our clinicians to offer unhurried appointments focused entirely on your respiratory care. While we do not bill insurance providers directly and coverage policies differ between insurers, many private health insurers reimburse our consultation and diagnostic testing fees. Following your appointment, practice manager Sofia Lindqvist provides an itemised receipt containing clinician credentials, diagnostic details, and procedure codes. You can submit this official receipt to your insurer to claim allowable benefits under your personal plan.

Cancellation and payment
What is the cancellation and payment policy?

We understand that personal schedules change unexpectedly. If you need to alter or cancel an appointment, cancellation is free up to 24 hours before your scheduled time. Notice given less than 24 hours in advance may be subject to the standard consultation fee. Payment is due on the day of your visit, and we accept debit cards, credit cards, and bank transfers at reception. For the 6-week breathing rehabilitation course, payment can be arranged prior to the introductory session.

Book a first visit

pages.title: Stories
pages.content:
Composite stories

Stories

Reading how others found their way back to steady breathing can help you understand our clinical process. These composite stories represent typical patient journeys managed at Kaze Clinic.

Who stays with the case

A named nurse stays with every case: a call at two weeks, a review at six.

Meet the clinicians

Composite stories

Three journeys, names changed

These composite stories represent typical patient journeys managed at Kaze Clinic.

The Cough That Outlasted a Winter
Persistent Cough Recovery

This composite story illustrates the care of a school teacher who arrived at Kaze Clinic after nine weeks of continuous, exhausting coughing following a common cold. Over-the-counter syrups and short medication trials had failed to provide relief. During her 45-minute first consultation with Dr. Ines Halvorsen, same-day spirometry and FeNO testing revealed marked eosinophilic airway inflammation and post-viral bronchial sensitivity.

Together, they agreed on a targeted inhaled therapy plan and vocal pacing techniques. By her two-week telephone call with nurse Lena Park, the night coughing had subsided, and she returned to teaching with steady breathing.

Stairs Again
COPD Pulmonary Rehabilitation

In this composite account, a retired mechanic with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease found himself struggling with breathlessness whenever he walked up the stairs in his home. A full lung function assessment with respiratory physiologist Tomás Reyes defined his baseline capacities, after which he enrolled in our 6-week breathing rehabilitation course led by physiotherapist Priya Raman.

Through weekly sessions, he learned diaphragmatic breathing patterns, physical pacing, and gentle conditioning exercises. By his six-week clinical review, he was climbing stairs steadily without stopping, having rebuilt the practical stamina and confidence needed for his daily routines.

Nights Without Waking
Sleep Breathing Support

A night-shift worker contacted Kaze Clinic describing persistent morning exhaustion, heavy headaches, and frequent nighttime awakenings that affected his concentration. Dr. Kwame Asante arranged an overnight home sleep study using a lightweight respiratory polygraphy kit used in the patient's own bed for one night. The recorded data confirmed repetitive airflow restriction and oxygen dips during sleep.

Dr. Asante explained the tracings clearly and coordinated a prompt referral for nocturnal breathing support alongside sleep position adjustments. Supported by follow-up calls from our nursing team, the patient achieved restful sleep and restored daytime alertness.

pages.title: Visit
pages.content:
Find us

Visit

Kaze Clinic is located in a quiet, accessible setting on Linden Walk in Northmere. We offer step-free access, reserved parking, and clear transport links for your appointment.

Getting here

Find the clinic

18 Linden Walk, Northmere
Phone: 020 5550 1420
Email: hello@kazeclinic.example

Location and public transport
Bus stop 80 m away

Our clinic is located at 18 Linden Walk, Northmere, in a peaceful neighborhood designed to provide a calm clinical environment. Reaching us by public transport is straightforward: the local bus stop 'Linden Walk' is situated just 80 m from our entrance, served by regular Northmere bus connections. If you are travelling by rail, local stations connect conveniently to Linden Walk by brief bus or taxi links. Our low-rise building features clear, legible signs and an inviting reception area with large windows, pale oak seating, and natural daylight.

Step-free access and parking
Two accessible bays

Ensuring unhindered, comfortable access for patients experiencing breathing difficulties is a fundamental design priority at Kaze Clinic. Our building offers a completely level, step-free entrance from the pavement with wide doorways suitable for wheelchairs and walking aids. Directly beside the front entrance, we provide 2 accessible parking bays reserved exclusively for patients attending consultations. Additional parking is available along Linden Walk. Inside the clinic, all consulting rooms, diagnostic suites, and patient facilities are situated on the ground floor with wide corridors and smooth, level flooring throughout.

Opening hours

Clinic opening hours and follow-up times

Kaze Clinic is open Monday to Friday from 08:30 to 18:00, with an extended Thursday evening clinic running until 20:00 to accommodate work and family commitments. On Saturday, we are open for morning appointments from 09:00 to 12:30. We are closed on Sundays and public holidays. Our clinical team conducts scheduled follow-up phone calls between 17:30 and 18:00 on weekdays, giving patients on active treatment plans a dependable daily opportunity to discuss their symptoms, review medication routines, and ask questions.

posts.title: Why we measure before we prescribe
posts.excerpt: At Kaze Clinic in Northmere, we perform objective lung function testing before initiating or altering respiratory treatment so every decision is anchored in physiological data.
posts.content:
When someone experiences persistent coughing, wheezing, or uncharacteristic breathlessness during normal activity, the most common clinical response is a trial prescription. A patient sits down for ten minutes, describes a tight chest, and walks away with an inhaler canister and instructions to see how they feel in a month. When Dr. Ines Halvorsen founded Kaze Clinic in 2014, she established a different standard for Northmere: respiratory care should always begin with objective physiological measurement, never guesswork.

The human respiratory system produces similar symptoms across fundamentally different conditions. Breathlessness can stem from variable smooth muscle constriction in asthma, irreversible loss of alveolar elasticity in COPD, post-viral airway hyperresponsiveness, or disordered breathing patterns. Prescribing an inhaled corticosteroid without verifying whether airway inflammation actually exists frequently leads to months of ineffective treatment. Conversely, withholding anti-inflammatory medicine because a stethoscope exam sounded clear can allow chronic bronchial irritation to progress unchecked.

This is why we measure first. During a 45-minute first consultation at our clinic, spirometry is performed on the same day by our respiratory physiologist, Tomás Reyes. By having a patient blow forcefully into a calibrated sensor, we measure forced expiratory volume and vital capacity. When airflow limitation is detected, we administer a bronchodilator and retest to assess reversibility. Coupled with FeNO testing, which measures fractional exhaled nitric oxide to detect eosinophilic inflammation, we obtain a precise diagnostic signature before selecting a single medicine.

Having objective numbers transforms the consultation from a passive prescription into a collaborative agreement. When doctor and patient sit together looking at a printed flow-volume curve, the physiology becomes visible. We can point directly to where the airflow dips and explain exactly why walking up a hill produces that familiar chest tightness. In Step 03 of our clinical process, we write down a personalized care plan in plain English. You see your baseline numbers, the exact mechanism targeted by your medicine, and the specific daily routines recommended by our clinical pharmacist, Daniel Okoro.

Measurement also provides the only reliable benchmark for follow-up. In our model, a named nurse—such as respiratory nurse specialist Lena Park—stays with your case. Two weeks after your initial visit, we telephone you during our 17:30 to 18:00 call window to check how your lungs are responding. At six weeks, we welcome you back for a follow-up consultation and repeat spirometry. Comparing your new flow-volume curve to your baseline confirms whether the airways have opened and inflammation has quieted. We do not need to ask if you think the inhaler is working; the lung function curve provides clear, objective evidence.

Breathing is something you can measure, track, and steady. By taking the time to test before we prescribe, we eliminate unneeded medications, resolve persistent symptoms faster, and ensure you remain in control of your health. Whether you are dealing with a cough that has outlasted a winter or unexplained shortness of breath, careful measurement at 18 Linden Walk gives your lungs the thorough, unhurried care they deserve.

posts.title: A short checklist for pollen season
posts.excerpt: Five small things that make spring easier if pollen sets off your chest.
posts.content:
If pollen sets off wheeze or a tickly cough, a little preparation before the season starts helps more than a lot of reaction once it has.

Check that your preventer inhaler is in date and that you can use the device properly; bring it to a nurse review if you are unsure. Keep your reliever where you can reach it. Wash your hair at night on high-pollen days, and keep bedroom windows closed in the early morning.

If your plan does not mention pollen, ask us to add a line to it.

posts.title: What a home sleep study involves
posts.excerpt: One night, a small recorder, a finger sensor and a nasal cannula, in your own bed.
posts.content:
A home sleep study records your breathing, oxygen level and heart rate for one night, in your own bedroom. You collect the kit from Linden Walk in the afternoon and a nurse shows you how to wear it.

The recorder is the size of a phone. A soft tube sits under your nose, a clip on your finger reads oxygen, and a belt notes your chest movement. Most people sleep close to normally.

You bring the kit back the next morning, and Dr. Asante reviews the recording and explains the result at your follow-up.
